Along with the change of the downloadable report format, AWS also increased the granularity of the data in the report:\\\\n\\\\n* **Lowered carbon reporting threshold**: AWS has lowered the carbon reporting threshold from one decimal place to three decimal places, which means the carbon emission data is now available at 0.00X metric tons of CO2e, from the previous 0.X metric tons of CO2e. For example, you can now see your carbon emissions for Amazon EC2 usage in North America. While there is no industry standard for allocating carbon emissions for cloud usage to customers, the update to the v2.0 methodology leveraged existing standards to support the CCFT, including: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, GHG Protocol Product Standard, ISO 14040/44 (LCA), ISO 14067 (Carbon footprint of products) and ICT Sector Guidance.\\\\n\\\\nCustomers can read more in the full-length methodology document, but here is a brief overview of the approach:\\\\n\\\\nScope 1 Emissions (Direct) Overview for v2.0\\\\n\\\\nScope 1 includes direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by AWS, such as fuel combustion in backup generators at our data centers. ## One important heads-up first
The old **Customer Carbon Footprint Tool (CCFT)** in the Billing console — the thing most people still picture for this — was **deprecated on June 30, 2026**. It's been replaced by the standalone **AWS Sustainability service**, which doesn't need Billing console permissions and has real API/SDK access (CCFT never had a proper public API). So the answer below uses the current service.

## The API call
**`sustainability:GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions`** (boto3 `sustainability` client, `get_estimated_carbon_emissions`).

```
GroupBy: ["USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID", "SERVICE"]
TimePeriod: { Start: ..., End: ... }
Granularity: "MONTHLY"   # this is both the default and the smallest supported granularity — no daily/partial-month rows exist
EmissionsTypes: (optional — defaults to TOTAL_LBM_CARBON_EMISSIONS + TOTAL_MBM_CARBON_EMISSIONS; can also request Scope 1/2/3 split)
```
`GroupBy` only accepts `USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `REGION`, or `SERVICE` — combining the first two gives exactly the "by linked account and by service" cut you want. If you want to know the exact service labels before running it, `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissionsDimensionValues` with `Dimensions: ["SERVICE"]` will enumerate them for your account set.

## Which services show up as separate lines
Whatever services generated measurable emissions in each linked account — typically EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS, DynamoDB, etc. One quirk: CloudFront's emissions are broken out as their own "Global Services" line rather than tied to a region, but it still appears as its own service row. Since AWS lowered the reporting threshold to 0.001 MTCO2e, smaller services that used to get lumped into "other" now often show up individually.

## Granularity and data availability — this is the part that'll surprise them
- Minimum/only granularity is **monthly** — there's no way to get partial-month ("this month so far") numbers, because emissions estimates aren't computed until a month closes.
- AWS now publishes each month's data **15th–21st of the following month** (down from up to 3 months previously).
- Given today is **November 9–10, 2026**:
  - **November 2026 ("this month so far"):** no data at all, not even partial — won't appear until mid-December at the earliest, and then only as a full month.
  - **October 2026 ("last month"):** also **not published yet** — it's due Nov 15–21.
  - The most recent complete month actually available right now is **September 2026**.
- So a "last 12 months including this month" request will really return complete monthly rows from roughly **October 2025 through September 2026**, with October and November 2026 missing. 38 months of history are retained, so the trailing-12 window is in no danger of falling off the back end.

## What a member account would see running the identical call
This inherits AWS Organizations consolidated-billing behavior:
- **Management account:** gets the consolidated view — every linked member account's emissions for the time each account was actually part of the org.
- **Member account:** running the exact same `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions` call with `GroupBy USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID` will only ever see **its own account ID** in the results — it has no visibility into sibling accounts, regardless of how it groups the query.
